speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: asked	the Minister for Manpower (a) what is the current percentage of employers that have an inclusive or multiracial workforce; (b) what percentage of these employers have employment policies that proactively seek to have an inclusive, diverse or multiracial employee base; and (c) whether the Ministry requires employers to make a serious attempt to create an inclusive work environment, starting with their employment policy.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: asked	the Minister for Manpower (a) what measures does the Ministry have to respond to and investigate complaints of racial or religious discrimination at the workplace and in employers' hiring policies; (b) what powers does the Ministry have in enforcing such practices and under what circumstances will the Ministry enforce its powers; (c) over the past five years, what are the trends of complaints from workers over discrimination and hiring practices; (d) how can the Ministry get more employers to embrace and adopt the values of diversity and inclusiveness in their employment policies; and (e) what is the level of awareness among workers of TAFEP's role in handling discrimination at the workplace and how can this awareness be improved.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari
text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) between 2011 and 2015, what is the number of complaints that the Tripartite Alliance for Fair Employment Practices (TAFEP) has received on alleged discriminatory practices in the workplace; (b) what is the trend of alleged discriminatory practices by individuals, companies or employers which are based on race and religion; (c) what are the actions taken by TAFEP or the Ministry against companies where the discriminatory practices have been proven to have taken place; and (d) whether TAFEP is vested with sufficient authority to mediate or resolve discriminatory practices that are reported.

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
text: The Ministry of Manpower (MOM) takes a serious view of any form of workplace discrimination.

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
text: We expect all employers to adopt the principles of fair and merit-based employment, in line with the Tripartite Guidelines on Fair Employment Practices.

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
text: In a survey conducted by MOM in 2014, two in three firms reported that they implemented fair employment practices.

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
text: The majority of those who did not were planning to do so.

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
text: To tackle complaints about workplace discrimination, MOM works with our tripartite partners through the Tripartite Alliance for Fair and Progressive Employment Practices (TAFEP).

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
text: TAFEP, as the advocate and champion for fair employment practices, plays an active role in looking into such complaints and refers cases to MOM for investigation where warranted.

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
text: Most of them were about unfair hiring practices, including posting discriminatory job advertisements and asking inappropriate questions during job interviews.

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
text: The remaining concerned in-employment issues, such as poor grievance handling and lack of sensitivity in communicating company policies and practices.

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
text: Prior to 2014, TAFEP took an advisory approach in counselling employers who were involved in such complaints.

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
text: Even so, we have taken stronger actions to deter workplace discrimination.

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
text: While this twin approach of advisory and deterrence has been reasonably effective, we can certainly do more.

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
text: MOM and our tripartite partners recognise that the key to eliminating discrimination is to spread this fair and inclusive message to all workplaces.

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
text: TAFEP will also ramp up training for HR practitioners to ensure recruitment and selection are based on the principles of fair and merit-based hiring, and publicise best practices in this area.

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
text: We should not condone discrimination of any form, including race and religion, in the workplace.

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
text: We can succeed in eliminating workplace discrimination when everybody plays a part.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: It is very heartening to know that TAFEP and MOM take a very serious approach to this.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: However, we still hear of some feedback of discriminatory practices when it comes to hiring.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I did not quite catch the answer to my Parliamentary Question about the percentages of companies that are inclusive or diverse in their racial make-up.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: My second question is whether TAFEP will do a detailed study on the racial make-up and overall inclusivity of companies as well as Statutory Boards, mainly to focus on good practices that 	Page: 24 these companies or Statutory Boards may have.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Third, are there plans to enhance recognition or award schemes that positively affirm employers, companies or Statutory Boards that are inclusive and racially diverse in their employment?

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
text: The majority of those which did not, which is the one-third, were planning to do so.

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
text: With reference to the Member's question about doing the survey again, we do that every four years.

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
text: The last one that we did was in 2014, so the next one that we will be doing will be in 2018.

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
text: As for recognising firms with good practices, TAFEP recognises employers that have good practices in creating an inclusive and diverse workforce through its Exemplary Employer Award.

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
text: We are looking at six areas, mainly, age, race, gender, family responsibilities, religion and disabilities.

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
text: This award celebrates the achievements of outstanding organisations that have implemented good practices in these areas and fair and progressive inclusive employment practices.

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
text: TAFEP hopes to inspire many more firms to do so.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I note in the reply that MOM is coming up with enforcement measures to curtail Work Pass applications for foreign manpower.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: How effective has this measure been in terms of setting the right tone among employers and for them to adhere to non-discriminatory practices?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: In cases and conversations, we also often hear from employees or jobseekers on how employers tend to favour or discriminate against certain race profiles and so forth.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Based on the findings that the Minister of State mentioned earlier on, are they mostly minority Singaporeans in this case, and how do we bridge that perception between employers and jobseekers, for example, because employers will also say they cannot find suitable Singaporeans or people of a certain race?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Last question, in terms of hiring practices, one fallout I can see, if you hit them too hard, is that there could be pre-emptive filtering, which means that even before they get to the hiring or interview table, they get filtered.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: How does MOM plan to look at these practices?

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
text: So far, we may investigate a certain case and after the investigation, we have issued warnings.

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
text: It is a very positive outcome after we implemented some of the penalties.

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
text: In terms of bridging the perception, MOM and our tripartite partners recognise that to eliminate discrimination, we need to spread the fair and inclusive employment practices message far, wide and deep.

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
text: We will also continue to step up the public education awareness.

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
text: Although the numbers remain stable, we know that, sometimes, you cannot eliminate all such cases.

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
text: We have to continue to drive hard, drive the message out clearly.

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
text: So, we are going to step up on public education.

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
text: We are going to make people more aware and conscious, especially between the employers and 	Page: 25 employees.

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
text: As for the recruitment practices, so far, individuals who know of such discrimination have approached TAFEP and informed us, and we would then start the investigation.

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
text: On strengthening recruitment and hiring practices, TAFEP usually advises the companies to implement best HR practices and make sure there is compliance.

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
text: Not only that, we are going to step up training for HR practitioners to ensure recruitment and selection are based on the principles of fair and merit-based hiring, and also publicise and share these best practices across all sectors.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: For those companies that MOM has given warnings to, how do you ensure compliance?

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
text: In the process of investigation, we make sure that the companies rectify all their practices, especially to make sure that the non-compliance issues are rectified and they comply with the fair employment practices.

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
text: Thereafter, TAFEP will share with and advise or counsel the employers on some of the good HR practices to make sure that it is done and all is complied with.

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
text: We check back on them to make sure they comply.

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
text: So far, there have been no repeat cases.

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
text: We are glad that, so far, all companies have heeded our advice.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Does the Ministry intend to conduct a survey of employees and job applicants because, surely, that would be a more accurate way of determining if there are really discriminatory practices that are prevalent, rather than asking the employers, but to also regularly survey the employees?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The second question is on the enforcement powers.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Does the Government feel that there are sufficient enforcement powers because, if an employer is recalcitrant in the face of a warning, the Minister of State mentioned that the Ministry can curtail the Work Pass or threaten to curtail the Work Pass.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: But what about companies that do not depend on Work Passes, which have an entirely domestic workforce?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: That threat may not be useful to get them to comply.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Is the Ministry satisfied that the current enforcement powers are sufficient to deal with such cases?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Even if such cases have not occurred now, they may occur in the future.

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
text: As for whether there is enough enforcement that is effective, if you look at the numbers so far, there are about 400 complaints of all sorts of discrimination, not just race and religion.

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
text: Between 2011 and 2015, on average, they made up about 400 of all the complaints.

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
text: Especially when we look at the outcome, all the companies heeded the advice and there were no repeated cases.

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
text: We will continue to monitor closely whether there are any such needs to increase the enforcement.

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
text: As of now, we feel that the current multi-pronged practice has been effective.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: A further supplementary question for the Minister of State regarding TAFEP's enforcement measures and what the Government can do to promote fair employment practices.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Would the Minister of State consider making it a requirement for participating in Government tenders or public sector tenders, that the company applying has a clean record with TAFEP and subscribes to fair employment practices?

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
text: For fair employment practices under the Code of Conduct, we need a tripartite agreement.

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
text: So, we will take the Member's suggestion back for a tripartite discussion and look at some of the alignments before considering that to be part of the condition for tenders.
